normalized.prelim_summary: This 2008 NC Miata Grand Touring has just 17k miles, a clean Carfax, and a rare Suspension Package with Bilstein shocks and a limited-slip differential. The seller has documented recent service and detailing extensively, with no reported mechanical or structural issues. It's a well-optioned, well-documented example of an early NC Miata in a desirable color combo.

critical_evidence.evidence: The listing and seller say a 2026 coolant flush was done and the expansion tank replaced with an aftermarket unit. The engine bay photo looks clean, but no receipt is shown. The radiator is presumably the original 18-year-old unit with plastic end tanks. Carfax has no reported coolant entry.
No scan or readiness data. Ohio emissions passes through 07/01/2024 suggest the car was compliant then, but nothing is current. The seller states the engine is stock.
The listing has top-up and top-down videos (not examined here). The photos show an intact tan top. There are no photos of the floor carpet or pad and no drain test.

One attached photo shows a clean rear subframe, diff and suspension mounts. Rockers, front subframe and wheel wells were not examined here. The seller says the car never saw winter roads; that is a claim only, in a salt-belt car.
The seller says he changed 'all the fluids (including drivetrain)', plus spark plugs and the serpentine belt. No receipts are shown, and Carfax has no reported transmission or diff entries.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: VIN, window sticker photo, and a Carfax with continuous Ohio registrations, an emissions-test mileage trail and documented July 2026 tires. The maintenance half is mostly claimed. Dealer records, oil notes and 2026 fluid, plug, belt and cooling receipts are said to exist but are not shown.

condition.rationale: Photos show near-new paint, a clean interior with only light bolster creasing, a tidy engine bay and a clean rear underside. Fresh tires are date-documented by Carfax. Still open: original radiator, 18-year-old dampers, early-6MT synchros, roof drains, and no scan or PPI.

price_value.rationale: The current $10,984 bid will rise. The likely hammer sits near the $14,129-$16,836 fair-value band, and no known-work items are established. That is fair value for a low-mile, well-optioned example rather than a bargain.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual, LSD, durable MZR drivetrain, likely inside the $10-19k ideal band, easy to resell. A strong enthusiast-bridge fit, now that the Miata is back in consideration.

logistics.rationale: Ohio, about 2,300 mi from Carmel, with a two-day auction window. A PPI before money moves would need to be arranged quickly through a Cleveland-area shop with seller agreement. California smog looks feasible for a stock car.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits together: Copper Red over tan, Grand Touring with the relatively rare Suspension Package and LSD, 6-speed, 17k miles, window sticker. The reversible Kenwood head unit and painted trim are minor, and the factory parts are included.

positives: The Carfax corroborates very low use with a consistent mileage trail (emissions passes at 9k-14k, 2012-2022) and one long-term owner from 2009 to 2026.
Desirable spec confirmed by the window sticker: Grand Touring, 6-speed, Suspension Package with LSD and Bilsteins, Premium Package, Copper Red over tan.
New Continental DWS 06 Plus tires and an alignment check are documented by Carfax (07/17/2026).
Photos show a clean rear underside and an excellent cosmetic condition. The car is mechanically stock per the seller and the factory stereo and trim are included.
No reported accidents and no title brand. Ohio emissions compliance through 2024 supports California smog feasibility.
concerns: Observed: Carfax shows a loan/lien reported 07/17/2026. The seller says it was paid off mid-September, but the title and lien release are not shown.
Observed: an aftermarket coolant expansion tank and an aftermarket Kenwood head unit with rear camera wiring. The tank brand and quality and the stereo install quality are unknown.

Unverified: the claimed 2026 coolant flush, drivetrain fluids, plugs and belt have no receipts shown, and the radiator is likely original at 18 years (ask for invoices; inspect the radiator end tanks).
Unverified: early-NC 6MT 2nd/3rd synchro behaviour (inspect with fast warm 2-3 shifts) and the condition of the 18-year-old Bilstein dampers and bushings.
Unverified: soft-top drains and floor dryness, and a current OBD readiness status (ask for a scan and photos under the carpet).
unknowns: Receipts for the 2026 work and the owner-1 Mazda dealer records

ppi_focus: Radiator end tanks, aftermarket expansion tank fitment and cap, and a cooling-system pressure test
OBD scan for codes and readiness, and confirmation of a stock ECU calibration
Fast 2-3 and 3-4 shifts at operating temperature for synchro grind; clutch engagement height and slave cylinder dampness
LSD behaviour on tight turns and the diff pinion and axle seals
Bilstein damper leakage and rebound, plus control-arm bushings, ball joints and end links on an 18-year-old chassis
Soft-top drains, the floor pan under the carpet, seat-track bolts and the rear window seal
Rockers, rear subframe, wheel wells and brake lines for salt-belt corrosion despite the no-winter claim
Kenwood and rear camera wiring quality and parasitic drain; condition of the new battery
Valve cover gasket and spark plug tube seals; evidence the plugs were actually replaced
what_would_change_verdict: Posted receipts for the 2026 cooling, fluid, plug and belt work, plus owner-1 dealer records, would move documentation into the 8 range.
A clean Cleveland-area PPI with OBD readiness, dry floors and no synchro grind before close would materially de-risk the car.
Evidence of floor-pan corrosion, radiator seepage, synchro grind or an unresolved lien would move it down sharply.
A hammer well above the fair-value band would erode price value.
evidence.mission_note: A 6-speed LSD NC with a durable Mazda drivetrain, likely to sell inside the $10-19k ideal band and easy to resell in 6-24 months, so it squarely fits the enthusiast-bridge brief. The two-day auction window constrains inspection timing under accelerated_bridge discipline.
evidence.rationale: The Carfax establishes identity, two owners, no reported accidents or brand, and a coherent low-mileage trail from 3,125 mi in 2009 to 16,077 last reported. That trail agrees with the listing's 17k miles and roughly 2k under the current owner. The window sticker confirms a well-optioned Grand Touring 6MT with the Suspension Package and LSD. July 2026 tires and an alignment check are documented. Photos show excellent paint and interior, a tidy engine bay, and a clean rear subframe. What remains claimed only is the seller's 2026 catch-up work (coolant flush, aftermarket expansion tank, all fluids including drivetrain, plugs, belt) and the previous owner's dealer records, none of which are posted. The radiator, the dampers and the early-6MT synchros are unaddressed age items. Carfax also shows a July 2026 lien, which the seller says is paid off but is not yet documented. Rockers, wheel wells, floor dryness and OBD readiness were not examined here.
evidence.next_action: Today, ask the seller in the BaT comments for the 2026 receipts, the lien release and a title photo, and permission for a Cleveland-area PPI with OBD scan before Friday's close; book an inspector for Thursday.
